name: Vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia, type cblDv2
aliases: Vitamin B12-responsive methylmalonic acidemia cblD subtype

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Biochemical and genetic diagnostic criteria for cblD methylmalonic acidemia

criteria.description: Elevated methylmalonic acid levels in plasma or urine
Clinical and biochemical improvement following vitamin B12 supplementation
Identification of pathogenic variants in the MMADHC gene
Normal or borderline serum vitamin B12 levels despite metabolic abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of elevated methylmalonic acid with clinical and biochemical response to vitamin B12 supplementation plus identification of pathogenic MMADHC gene variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of biochemical, clinical, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Severe metabolic acidosis due to organic acid accumulation
Detected via urine organic acid analysis
searchTerms: high levels of methylmalonic acid in urine
elevated organic acid in urine tests

pathognomonic.notes: Improvement of biochemical abnormalities upon B12 therapy
searchTerms: metabolic problems fixed by vitamin B12

common.notes: Delayed acquisition of motor and cognitive milestones
Reduced muscle tone observed in infancy
Macrocytic anemia due to impaired DNA synthesis

occasional.notes: Elevated blood ammonia levels secondary to metabolic dysfunction

rare.notes: Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy reported in rare cases
Hearing impairment due to nerve involvement

laboratory: Elevated methylmalonic acid in plasma and urine
Normal or borderline serum vitamin B12 levels
imaging: Brain MRI may show cerebral atrophy or delayed myelination
other: Positive biochemical response to parenteral hydroxocobalamin therapy

distinguishingFeatures: Often combined methylmalonic acidemia and homocystinuria

redFlags: Severe metabolic ketoacidosis in neonate or infant
Poor response to standard vitamin B12 doses without genetic confirmation
Rapid neurological deterioration with metabolic crises
references: Fowler B, Leonard JV, Baumgartner MR. Causes of and diagnostic approach to methylmalonic acidurias. J Inherit Metab Dis. 2008;31(3):350-360.
Watkins D, Rosenblatt DS. Inherited disorders of cobalamin absorption and metabolism. Am J Med Genet C Semin Med Genet. 2011;157C(1):33-44.
